recognize_zh: 上方為含空泡、細胞碎屑與退化嗜中性球的壞死帶，下方為排列成漩渦狀、胞核細長的類上皮組織球層，兩者交界清楚，屬壞死性肉芽腫的邊緣。
features: Sharp interface between a necrotic zone (top) and a granulomatous rim (bottom)
Necrotic zone with nuclear debris, degenerating neutrophils and foamy/vacuolated histiocytes with clear spaces
Epithelioid histiocytes with elongated, oval to spindle, vesicular nuclei in a swirling pattern with abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm
Scattered small lymphocytes among the histiocytes
No giant cells, organisms or atypical large cells evident in this field
describe_en: Section of lymph node at medium power shows the edge of a necrotizing granuloma. The upper portion consists of necrotic debris with degenerating neutrophils, nuclear fragments and vacuolated histiocytes, and is bordered by a band of epithelioid histiocytes with elongated vesicular nuclei arranged in a vaguely palisading, swirling pattern with interspersed lymphocytes. No organisms or cytologically malignant cells are identified on H&E. Findings are consistent with necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis; AFB and fungal stains and microbiologic correlation are recommended.

ddx.vs: Cat-scratch lymphadenitis typically has stellate microabscesses with central neutrophils and palisading histiocytes plus monocytoid B-cell hyperplasia; confirmation requires Warthin-Starry stain, PCR or serology.
Kikuchi lacks neutrophils and palisading epithelioid granulomas, instead showing karyorrhectic debris with crescentic histiocytes and CD123+ plasmacytoid dendritic cells.
Fungal infection may look identical on H&E and is distinguished by GMS/PAS demonstration of yeast forms.
